captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/33_pirl, specifically its ResNet-50 step 1 (models/resnet_pirl.py, loss/memory_nce.py, data/pirl_dataset.py, train_step1_pirl.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Misra & van der Maaten (CVPR 2020) PIRL. torchvision supplies ResNet-50; there is no submodule and no timm, so this ports self-contained and torch-only. The port keeps the capture directory numbering (33) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (this list's number 14 is PIRL -- see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).
scope: The ResNet-50 step 1 is ported: a ResNet-50 trunk (torchvision, up to and including avgpool) encodes an image and a jigsaw-shuffled view of the same image; the image goes through a 2048->128 projector, and the nine jigsaw patches go through the same trunk + projector, are concatenated (9x128) and projected to 128 dims. Both representations are L2-normalised and contrasted against a momentum-updated memory bank (one row per training image) with an NCE cross-entropy (the positive is the image's own bank row, plus num_negatives random negatives). The loss is a convex combination (1 - jigsaw_weight) * image-NCE + jigsaw_weight * jigsaw-NCE; the bank is updated with the image representation each step. The bank is optionally seeded from the model's features before training. The capture's step 2 (ViT) is EXCLUDED, as in every port.
encoder: encoder.pt is the ResNet-50 trunk (encoder.*): the torchvision resnet50 up to and including avgpool, producing a 2048-d feature. The image projector (projector.*), the jigsaw projector (jigsaw_projector.*) and the memory bank are excluded -- the bank is a register_buffer in the loss module (PIRLMemoryBankNCE), not in the model, so it is never in model.state_dict (the instance-discrimination convention). The standard SSL convention of probing the backbone, the same shape as the 10_inst_disc port.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the ResNet-50 trunk (2048-d, avg-pooled) via get_encoder(), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation -- the same normalisation PIRL trains with). Follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own head, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.
rewritten_during_the_port: only the ResNet-50 step 1 is ported; the capture's step 2 (ViT) is excluded, as in every port (so no timm)

the ResNet-50 model with image + jigsaw projection heads, the memory-bank NCE loss (with its EMA bank update), the jigsaw view (resize -> crop -> 3x3 cells -> per-cell random patch -> colour jitter -> shuffle) and the convex-combination loss are kept faithfully (all torch)
the DistributedSampler is dropped (single-process) and a seeded generator is threaded so a run is reproducible; the DDP all_gather in the memory update is kept but inert single-process
image_size and the jigsaw geometry are threaded so a small hermetic CPU smoke runs at a lower resolution
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the capture called .cuda())
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)

the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel and TensorBoard/tqdm so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32; the SGD step-milestone LR schedule (with optional warmup) and the memory-bank initialisation from the model are kept
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; step-1 reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
